The action therefore waits for a resolved identity and for the ADR that names a mesh event's human author. Proposed in ADR <n1/> (The persistent runtime is the authority; every operator surface, Lumen included, is a client of it); ADR <n2/> (Prismatic Lumen names the owner's mesh-wide view, and it owns no scheduler, event bus, store or API) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). Sources: chatgpt-majordomus:c296#18.

en: Open the repository in one MCP client and majordomus mcp is the server: its stdio serves that client, and beside it a loopback socket serves a home page listing every surface, this repository's documentation at /docs/, Swagger UI at /swagger, the OpenAPI document, every capability route and MCP over HTTP at /mcp; the URL and every surface are in the log the moment it is bound. Open the repository in a second client and its majordomus mcp does not start another server: it finds the first through the lease, checks that it answers for this root, and forwards its client's frames to it. Close the clients in any order and the server lingers exactly as long as one is attached; when the last leaves it closes the port and removes the lease. Kill the server and a bridged client takes its place, or attaches to whichever process took the lease first, and its own client never re-initialises. --standalone serves one client alone with no port and no lease.

Otevřete repozitář v druhém klientovi a jeho majordomus mcp nespouští další server: najde první přes lease, ověří, že odpovídá za tento kořen, a předává mu rámce svého klienta. Zavírejte klienty v libovolném pořadí a server zůstane přesně tak dlouho, dokud je připojen jeden; když odejde poslední, zavře port a odstraní lease. Zabijte server a přemostěný klient nastoupí na jeho místo nebo se připojí k procesu, který lease získal první, a jeho vlastní klient se nikdy znovu neinicializuje. --standalone obsluhuje jediného klienta bez portu a bez lease.

en: This repository models the work: milestones are outcomes, issues are execution contracts, commits trace to issues and claims trace to recorded runs.
